title: Never Outshine the Master
coreMove: Route visible excellence through the superior's status before comparison turns skill into threat
sourcePressure: why visible excellence becomes dangerous when it humiliates the person above you, and why redirected credit can convert the same excellence into protection.

sourceAnchors.name: Nicolas Fouquet
sourceAnchors.detail: staged a spectacular display before Louis XIV and was punished after the king felt overshadowed
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Fouquet shows the danger of making the person above you feel small inside his own room.

sourceAnchors.name: Galileo
sourceAnchors.detail: framed scientific achievement so the Medici family felt elevated and protected by association
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Galileo kept the brilliance but changed where the credit landed.

sourceAnchors.name: Louis XIV
sourceAnchors.detail: the superior whose status threat turns Fouquet's magnificence into danger
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Louis XIV matters here less as a monarch than as a superior forced into public comparison.
